title: Compactness for bounded families from single-degree compactness
statement: Let A be an abelian category with K-injective resolutions and a chosen ordinary derived category D(A). Fix an index type J and suppose coproducts indexed by J exist in A. Let P be an isomorphism-closed class of objects of A containing a zero object, and let s be an object of D(A). Suppose that for every integer n and family B : J -> A with B_j in P, every morphism s -> coproduct_j B_j[-n] is a finite sum of morphisms through the coprojections. Then, for every natural number d, integer a and family K : J -> D(A) with all cohomology in P and supported in [a,a+d], every morphism s -> coproduct_j K_j is a finite sum of morphisms through the coprojections. Single-degree objects, the chosen derived category and standard truncations are those of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category; lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology].

source.place: Proof, induction on b-a; already implemented by WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.CompactOfBoundedExt.compactFor_of_isGE_of_isLE

proof.text: For width zero, each K_j is isomorphic to its degree-a cohomology sheaf placed in degree a. This follows from the standard t-structure single-object characterization; the cohomology of the isomorphism identifies that sheaf with H^a(K_j), so it belongs to P by repleteness. The assumed single-degree compactness and invariance under family isomorphisms give the base case.

For the successor width d+1 set b=a+d+1 and use the standard truncation triangle tau_<b K_j -> K_j -> tau_>=b K_j. The first terms have cohomology in P and bounds [a,a+d], because truncation retains or kills cohomology and P contains zero. The third terms have bounds [b,b] and cohomology in P. Apply the induction hypothesis and the width-zero case, respectively.

Coproducts of these distinguished triangles are distinguished, as in the proved source-library CompactFor.of_distTriang. Given a map from s to the middle coproduct, compactness on the third family expresses its image as finitely many components. Each component has zero boundary: composing the summed boundary with the coordinate projection recovers that component. Hom exactness lifts each component to a middle-term morphism. Subtract their finite sum; the difference lifts from the first coproduct, whose compactness writes it as another finite sum. Add the two finite expressions. This proves compactness of the middle family and completes induction, including empty families.

lemma compactFor_of_isGE_of_isLE {s : DerivedCategory C}
    (hsum : ∀ (n : ℤ) (B : J → C), (∀ j, P (B j)) →
      CompactFor s fun j ↦ (singleFunctor C n).obj (B j)) (d : ℕ) :
    ∀ (a : ℤ) (K : J → DerivedCategory C) (_ : ∀ j, homologyProperty P (K j))
      [∀ j, (K j).IsGE a] [∀ j, (K j).IsLE (a + d)], CompactFor s K
